protectedFieldsNote: Article 55A.253(a) requires the petition to carry sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, social security number and the address at the time of arrest, and the TRN must appear on the order under art. 55A.301. All of them are blank here and are never prefilled by any pipeline stage. How the largest counties handle sensitive data in a public civil expunction filing is a recorded release blocker; the participant supplies these by hand.

expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA. Each ground is either a prohibited term for this track or prohibited invention. (1) Prohibited terms: the output says the record 'will be sealed' and names 'the nondisclosure statute'. Nondisclosure is Gov't Code ch. 411 relief, a different remedy in a different code with a different venue — the sentencing court rather than the county of arrest. A Chapter 55A pleading that uses sealing or nondisclosure vocabulary is the wrong remedy on its face. (2) The offence date is 10/01/2022, after 2021-09-01. The recorded exclusion is 'an offence committed on or after 2021-09-01'. This participant is not eligible on this route at all. (3) The subsection is 46.02(a-1), and the screening answer is 'not sure'. The route reaches 46.02(a) as it existed before 2021-09-01 and no other subsection, and 'any conviction where the offence date and the statutory subsection cannot be confirmed from court records' is a recorded exclusion and a self-help stop condition. (4) It proceeds despite abscondedAfterRelease = yes, a recorded stop condition; art. 55A.154 makes an intentional or knowing absconder ineligible and the registry states a participant may not self-identify the fact. (5) It fills court identity no source supplies: cause number, judicial district and judge name. The matter is a NEW civil action that receives a NEW cause number on filing. (6) It states a position for the attorney representing the state — an outside-party act no source records. (7) It asserts service completion by the petitioner. The CLERK serves under art. 55A.254; the participant does not serve in the ordinary case. (8) It asserts a hearing date and a hearing outcome, both court acts. (9) It quotes a filing fee of $325.00 when the county figure is an open release blocker and the old $250-$500 range is expressly disavowed. (10) It populates every art. 55A.253(a) protected identifier and the TRN, all of which must stay blank. (11) It alleges a 5-year waiting period. Article 55A.005 states none, and the 5-year figure belongs to the Gov't Code nondisclosure subtypes, not to Chapter 55A. (12) It says relief happens 'automatically'. There is no automatic route for art. 55A.005; the only automatic expunction entry recorded anywhere on the Texas denominator is art. 55A.202 for art. 55A.003 actual-innocence pardons.
